newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on low volumes again.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on low volumes again.

text.p: COMEX gold and silver futures ended lower Thursday, while NYMEX platinum and palladium ended higher in another day of narrow ranges and light volumes, traders said.
Activity focused mainly on silver's May/July roll, with the July contract taking over as the most active this week with more open interest.

"If it wasn't for the silver spreads, volumes would have been even lower, with funds and trade houses just trying to take advantage of both sides of the narrow ranges," FIMAT New York metals trader, John Tyree, said.

COMEX May silver ended down 3.2 cents at $4.693 an ounce, after trading a narrow $4.730-4.675 range. COMEX July silver ended down 3.28 cents also at $4.741 an ounce, after trading a $4.775-4.725 range. Estimated total volume in COMEX silver was 35,000 lots.

Open interest in COMEX silver has declined this week to 96,764 contracts Wednesday, from an eight-month high at 102,323 lots last Thursday, after silver prices slid back below $5.00 in early April to test the two year lows seen in January.
July silver's five-day (weekly) moving-average remains below its 21-day (monthly) average and its 55-day (quarterly) average, suggesting the downtrend has not reversed yet, analysts said.
But the selloff looks like it may have come to an end, with support found again around $4.700 in the July contract this week, analysts said.
Silver's fundamentals are still been better than gold's this year, with fabrication demand seen outstripping newly refined silver supply for the eighth year in a row.

The amount of silver bullion available to the market is believed to be at its lowest levels in about 46 years, with inventories representing less than seven months of silver use, according to New York industry analysts, CPM Group.
The spot gold/silver ratio was little changed around 72.6 Thursday, after recovering in the past two months from a 22-month low in February at 66.1.
COMEX June gold ended down 60 cents at $342.70 an ounce, after trading a $344.00-342.00 range. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was only 12,000 lots.

Open interest in COMEX gold is little changed so far this week at 163,216 lots Wednesday, after recovering from a 12-month low at 148,359 lots on April 8, as gold slid back to test its four year lows last week.

Gold also appears to have found some support this week just above $340 an ounce in the June contract, and volatility measures have slipped further. Twenty day historical volatility slipped back below eight percent Thursday.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $340.50/00, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $340.90 and the New York close Wednesday around $341.10/60.
But gold equities took another tumble, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's index of North American gold and silver stocks (.XAU) sliding to new four year lows at 91.18 near the close.
A strong U.S. dollar and rising U.S. interest rates are seen limiting the demand for gold by investors on the one hand and is pressuring producer profitability on the other, analysts said.

The Australian dollar price of gold is back down around $438.00 an ounce, testing the five year lows seen in March, while the South African rand price, around 1,511 rand an ounce, is back down near its lowest levels in a year.
South African gold miners are threatening to cut jobs and close some mines as a result of the weak gold price.
Anglo American Corp said Thursday losses at shafts within its Free State Consolidated Gold Mines (Freegold) were unsustainable and the shafts might close.
Freegold is the world's biggest gold mine.
Anglo American reported a 34 percent drop in March quarter profit Thursday.
The outlook for platinum group metals was healthier, with no sign yet of a resumption of Russian supplies to Japan and the physical market very tight, traders said.
Platinum and palladium short term lease rates remained high around 10-12 percent for both metals, refining sources said.
NYMEX July platinum ended up $1.40 an ounce at $375.80, while NYMEX June palladium gained 45 cents to settle at $155.45.
